newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: New U.N. arms chief Butler heads for Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: New U.N. arms chief Butler heads for Baghdad.

text.p: Richard Butler, the U.N. official in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction, headed for Baghdad on Monday for talks with Iraqi officials, a United Nations spokesman said.
Butler, an Australian, took over as chairman of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) on Iraq this month. He replaced Sweden's Rolf Ekeus, who built up UNSCOM in 1991.
Butler arrived in Bahrain, headquarters of U.N. missions visiting Baghdad, from New York on Sunday night. He is expected to return to the island on July 27.
Bahrain's Gulf Daily News quoted Butler as saying he hoped to complete his Baghdad mission as soon as possible.
"This will require major progress, especially in the field of biological and chemical weapons," he was quoted as saying.
UNSCOM must certify that Baghdad has no weapons of mass destruction before the United Nations will lift sanctions imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
